handoff: No blocking findings. AC1-AC4 proven (pr-evidence integration test + rawFileUrl contract on gh/glab/FakeRemote); AC5 is a person check, how-to in the handoff. 9 minor/nit findings: link-regex edge cases, resolver checks the live dir not the record tree, lease on an unfetched ref, no decide-seam case for the push_record suppression, per-link repo view, JSDoc placement. Unit 1215 pass, typecheck green.

findings.title: Slice-unit link not proven at S1
findings.detail:
AC1's example is a slice link (evidence/01-parser/<run_id>/shot.png). The integration test covers only _story. recordLinkResolver's slice branch is exercised only through a stub resolver in record-links.test.ts.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a slice-unit link case at S1, or a resolver test over a real machine-dir layout.

findings.title: Dot-folders now skipped in rulings too
findings.detail:
storyRecord adds !d.name.startsWith('.'), and rulings() uses it, which changes existing rulings behaviour. Harmless, but not asked for.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep it, and note it in the PR.

findings.title: Rewrites inside code spans/fences; reference-style links not rewritten
findings.detail:
The spec says nothing about either. RECORD_LINK matches `](evidence/` and `src="evidence/` anywhere, fenced code included, and skips `[x]: evidence/...` definitions. On rework the rewrite stays idempotent, because pr.md keeps its raw paths and the body is rebuilt from it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Optionally skip code spans and fences, and support reference definitions.

findings.title: Link regex edge cases
findings.detail:
An angle-bracket target with a space (`](<evidence/_story/R/after shot.png>)`) is cut at the space. A ?query or #fragment is captured into the path. An agent-percent-encoded link is not decoded. In each case a real file is reported as missing.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Parse the <...> form up to '>', strip ?/# and decodeURIComponent before resolving.

findings.title: Resolver checks the live machine dir, not the pushed record tree
findings.detail:
statSync follows symlinks and accepts dot-named segments, but filesUnder (store record-ref.ts) leaves both out of the record. Such a link becomes a URL the record does not serve and is not named as missing. Evidence written after the pack has the same race.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Resolve against `git ls-tree -r <record sha>`.

findings.title: Lease on a local record ref that is never fetched
findings.detail:
expected is the local refs/norn/runs/<story>. fetchNornRefs does not fetch record refs, so if the local ref lags the remote (takeover under local), every open-pr retry fails as stale. The implementer flags this and defers it to the takeover slices (D10).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Confirm that the D10 takeover slices fetch the record ref.

findings.title: push_record suppression not covered at the decide seam
findings.detail:
No core unit test, rule-case or golden decides open-pr with an owed record under remote. Only pr-evidence.test.ts covers it. The suppression emits nothing, so the golden rule check cannot catch a regression (X4).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add a hand-built decide case: open-pr plus an owed record under remote decides no push_record.

findings.title: One `repo view` network call per distinct link
findings.detail:
rawFileUrl in gh (and glab/index.ts:157) runs `repo view` every time, so N links cost N network calls.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Memoise the repo URL in the adapter.

findings.title: encodePath separates portError from its JSDoc
findings.detail:
The 'Typed failure for port methods' doc comment now sits above encodePath. FakeRemote (test/support/harness.ts:96) inlines the same encoding, and git-step.ts:234 casts `record as string`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Move encodePath above the comment, and narrow instead of casting.
